definitions.explanation: A large structure with blades that rotate in the wind, used historically for grinding grain or pumping water, and now for generating electricity. Distinct from the toy pinwheel ({風車|かざぐるま}).

examples.japanese: オランダは{風車|ふうしゃ}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: The Netherlands is famous for its windmills.

examples.japanese: {風力発電|ふうりょくはつでん}の{風車|ふうしゃ}が{丘|おか}の{上|うえ}に{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Wind turbines are lined up on top of the hill.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では、{風車|ふうしゃ}を{使|つか}って{地下水|ちかすい}を{汲|く}み{上|あ}げる{仕組|しく}みが{昔|むかし}から{使|つか}われてきた。
examples.english: In this area, a system of using windmills to pump up groundwater has been used since ancient times.

notes:
READING NOTE:
The same kanji {風車|ふうしゃ} can also be read as かざぐるま, which means a toy pinwheel. The reading ふうしゃ refers to the large structure (windmill or wind turbine), while かざぐるま refers to the small toy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風車|ふうしゃ}{小屋|ごや} (windmill building)
- {風力発電|ふうりょくはつでん}の{風車|ふうしゃ} (wind power turbine)
- {風車|ふうしゃ}が{回|まわ}る (the windmill turns)
